questions.q: Asha taps the search box in the Bazaar app. Which part is she touching?
questions.explain: The frontend is the part you can see and touch, like buttons and the search box. The backend works behind it.

questions.q: The app sends price ₹1 for Red Running Shoes. What should Bazaar's backend do?
options: Accept it, because the app sent it
Use its own price from its own data, ₹999
Ask the phone to send the price again
questions.explain: Never trust the frontend. Anyone can change what an app sends, so the backend always uses its own data for prices and rules.

questions.q: Why doesn't the Bazaar app talk to the database directly?
options: The database password would be inside the app for anyone to find, and the rules would run where customers can change them
It would use too much battery
questions.explain: Secrets and rules must stay on the server. The backend is the one trusted place all frontends ask.

options: A special magic machine only big companies have
A normal computer whose job is to answer requests from other computers
questions.explain: A server is just a computer running programs that answer requests. In the lab, your own laptop acted as a server.

questions.q: Which of these is valid JSON?
questions.explain: JSON needs double quotes around keys and strings, and no comma after the last item.

questions.q: curl says "(52) Empty reply from server". What happened?
options: Nothing is listening on that port
The backend accepted the connection but crashed before sending an answer
questions.explain: Connection refused (error 7) means nobody is listening. Empty reply (52) means the backend was there but broke. Read its logs.

questions.q: In the restaurant analogy, what is the database?
options: The store room with the ingredients
questions.explain: The database is where data is stored safely, like a store room. The kitchen (backend) takes what it needs from there.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Bazaar answers with status code 503. What do you know immediately?
options: It is a 5xx code, so the problem is on the server's side
questions.explain: 2xx = success, 4xx = the client made a mistake, 5xx = the server made a mistake. Learn the families first.
